idiom_name: struct holding a PgPool; async query_as::<_, T> + FromRow
implementation_notes: The repository is a struct owning a connection pool (PgPool) with async methods returning Result<Option<Invoice>, sqlx::Error>; sqlx::query_as::<_, Invoice> with #[derive(FromRow)] replaces the hand-written mapper, and query_as! checks statements against a live schema at compile time. Model the interface as a trait (InvoiceRepository: Send + Sync) only when tests need an in-memory double, and prefer a concrete struct plus a narrow consumer-side trait otherwise. Transactions stay explicit: take &mut PgConnection or a Transaction by parameter so the repository never commits behind the caller's back.
pitfalls: sqlx::Error and row types must not leak into the domain: map them to a domain error at the boundary, or domain code depends on the driver crate.
Keep the Transaction on the caller's stack: it borrows a connection exclusively, and holding one across unrelated awaits starves the pool.
query_as! (compile-time checked) needs a live database or a prepared offline .sqlx cache in CI; without it clean checkouts fail to build.

variants.name: Diesel repository (sync DSL over a generated schema)
variants.idiom_name: struct holding a connection; Diesel DSL queries returning QueryResult<T>
variants.implementation_notes: Diesel puts the mapping in a code-generated schema module and the queries in a typed DSL: invoices::table.filter(invoices::due.lt(on)).load::<Invoice>(&mut conn), with #[derive(Queryable, Selectable, Insertable)] replacing the mapper. It is synchronous and connection-centric, which suits workers, CLIs and batch jobs but needs a blocking pool (tokio::task::spawn_blocking) inside async servers; the repository becomes a thin struct wrapping the connection with domain-language methods.
pitfalls: The generated schema ties the repository to the database layout at compile time: a migration without regenerating fails the build, which is intended but is real coupling.
Diesel is synchronous: calling it directly from async code blocks the executor; wrap it in a blocking pool.
Generic over Connection makes the repository testable on SQLite, but backend-specific SQL (RETURNING, ON CONFLICT) does not port - keep such queries behind a backend-specific impl.
